stories.title: Share Offer via Native Share Sheet
stories.user_story: As a consumer, I want to share an offer using my device's native share sheet, so that I can send it to friends through any messaging or social app I already use
acceptance_criteria: Given I am viewing an offer detail screen, When I tap the 'Share' button, Then the OS native share sheet opens with a pre-composed message containing the offer title, merchant name, and a deep link
Given the share sheet is open, When I select a target app and confirm, Then the share completes and a share event is recorded with offer_id, channel, and timestamp
Given the shared content, When it is received by the recipient, Then no personally identifiable information about the sharer is included in the message or deep link
Given a screen reader is active, When navigating the offer detail screen, Then the Share button announces 'Share this offer' and its action clearly
Given the share action fails (no network, cancelled), When the failure occurs, Then the app returns gracefully to the offer detail screen with no error unless network-related
stories.regulatory_linkage: GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) — data minimization (no PII in shared content)
stories.reasoning: Core sharing mechanic using platform-native share sheet. 3 points: native integration on both iOS/Android + event tracking + anonymity enforcement. Internal sensitivity as no PII is transmitted.

stories.title: Deep Link Resolution & Attribution Tracking
stories.user_story: As a consumer who received a shared offer link, I want to tap the link and land directly on the offer in the app, so that I can view and redeem it without searching
acceptance_criteria: Given I tap a shared offer deep link and have the app installed, When the app opens, Then I am navigated directly to the offer detail screen for the referenced offer
Given I tap a shared offer deep link and do not have the app installed, When the link resolves, Then I am directed to the appropriate app store listing
Given I arrived via a shared deep link, When the offer detail loads, Then the system records an attribution event linking this view to the original share event (without revealing sharer identity)
Given the deep link references an expired or invalid offer, When the app opens, Then I see a message 'This offer is no longer available' with a link to browse current offers
Given a screen reader is active, When the deep-linked offer detail loads, Then focus is placed on the offer title and the screen content is announced
stories.regulatory_linkage: GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) — anonymous attribution (no sharer PII stored with recipient data)

requirements_used: F-07.1 — Social Offer Sharing (deep link, attribution tracking, anonymous)

stories.reasoning: 5 points: universal/app link configuration on both platforms + deferred deep linking for non-installed case + attribution service + expired offer handling. Higher complexity due to cross-platform link routing and backend attribution logic.

stories.title: Post-Redemption Rating Prompt
stories.user_story: As a consumer who has just redeemed an offer, I want to be prompted to rate my experience, so that I can help other consumers find the best offers
acceptance_criteria: Given I have successfully redeemed an offer, When the redemption confirmation screen is displayed, Then a rating prompt appears after a 2-second delay showing 1–5 stars and 'How was this offer?'

Given the rating prompt is visible, When I tap a star (1–5), Then my rating is submitted, the prompt dismisses with a 'Thanks for your feedback' confirmation, and the rating is stored against the offer
Given the rating prompt is visible, When I tap 'Not now' or dismiss it, Then the prompt closes and does not reappear for this redemption
Given I have already rated this specific redemption, When I view the redemption history, Then my submitted rating is displayed (read-only)
Given a screen reader is active, When the rating prompt appears, Then each star is announced as 'Rate X out of 5 stars' and the selected state is conveyed

requirements_used: F-07.2 — Review-Based Recommendations (post-redemption rating prompt, 1-5 stars)

stories.reasoning: 2 points: simple UI prompt with star input + API call to store rating. Low complexity — single screen interaction with straightforward backend persistence.

stories.title: Rating-Based Offer Ranking & Moderation
stories.user_story: As a consumer browsing offers, I want offers to be ranked considering user ratings, so that highly-rated offers surface higher and poorly-rated ones are deprioritised
acceptance_criteria: Given an offer has an average rating ≥ 4.0 with at least 10 ratings, When the offer list is generated, Then the offer receives a ranking boost (weighted factor applied to relevance score)
Given an offer has an average rating ≤ 2.0 with at least 10 ratings, When the offer list is generated, Then the offer receives a ranking penalty (reduced visibility in results)

Given a newly submitted rating, When it is processed, Then the system checks for abuse patterns (same user rating same merchant repeatedly, burst of 1-star ratings) and flags suspicious ratings for moderation
Given a flagged rating is reviewed by the moderation system, When it is confirmed as abusive, Then it is excluded from the average calculation
Given a screen reader is active, When browsing the offer list, Then the average rating for each offer is announced as 'Rated X out of 5 stars based on N reviews'
stories.reasoning: 3 points: ranking algorithm adjustment + abuse detection heuristics + moderation exclusion logic. Medium complexity — backend scoring changes with basic fraud detection rules.

stories.title: Wearable Offer Notification Delivery
stories.user_story: As a consumer wearing an Apple Watch or Wear OS device, I want to receive nearby offer notifications on my wrist, so that I can see relevant offers without taking out my phone
acceptance_criteria: Given I have the companion app installed on my Apple Watch or Wear OS device and notifications are enabled, When a location-triggered offer notification fires, Then it is delivered to my wearable with offer title, merchant name, and discount summary
Given a notification is displayed on my wearable, When I view it, Then I see a clear 'Open on phone to redeem' action button
Given I tap 'Open on phone to redeem', When the action is triggered, Then the paired phone opens the app directly to the offer detail screen
Given I have notification permissions disabled for the wearable companion app, When a location-triggered offer fires, Then no wearable notification is sent and the phone notification is unaffected
Given VoiceOver (watchOS) or TalkBack (Wear OS) is active, When a notification arrives, Then the offer title, merchant, and action are announced audibly

requirements_used: F-07.3 — Wearable Device Notifications (Apple Watch/Wear OS companion, 'Open on phone to redeem')

stories.reasoning: 3 points: companion app notification routing on both watchOS and Wear OS + phone handoff action + permission handling. Medium complexity due to dual-platform wearable support.

stories.title: Wearable Complication for Active Offers
stories.user_story: As a consumer, I want a watch face complication showing my nearest active offer count, so that I can glance at my wrist to know if offers are available nearby
acceptance_criteria: Given I have added the offers complication to my watch face, When offers are available within my configured radius, Then the complication displays the count of nearby active offers (e.g., '3 offers')
Given no offers are available nearby, When the complication refreshes, Then it displays '0 offers' or a placeholder icon indicating no current offers
Given I tap the complication, When the companion app opens, Then I see a summary list of nearby offers with 'Open on phone to redeem' for each
Given the complication data is stale (>15 minutes since last update), When the next background refresh cycle runs, Then the count is updated from the phone's cached offer data
Given VoiceOver (watchOS) or TalkBack (Wear OS) is active, When the complication is focused, Then it announces 'X nearby offers available'
stories.reasoning: 2 points: complication UI is simple (count display) + background refresh from phone cache. Lower complexity than notification delivery — primarily a data display widget with periodic updates.
